title: Adani's Vizag hyperscale campus proceeds at developer's risk
source_used: W.Media (citing The Times of India); ET Datacenters original returned no text
key_facts: The Andhra Pradesh High Court said Vizag Hyperscale Data Centre Park Limited, an Adani Infra (India) special purpose vehicle, may proceed with building an AI-ready data centre campus in Visakhapatnam but at its own risk.
The project's future depends on a final decision in a public interest case challenging several approvals granted by the state government, according to The Times of India.
The campus is part of Google's AI hub in India, announced in October 2025 as part of an investment of about US$15 billion over five years.

Three petitions to the National Green Tribunal, reported by The Guardian in September, allege the environmental and water risk assessment was 'grossly inadequate, scientifically unrealistic, and misleading'.
Challengers also say the Kambalakonda Wildlife Sanctuary, less than a kilometre away, means central government approval was needed.
The court said investment now cannot be used as grounds for relief if the approvals are ruled improper.
quote_evidence: The Andhra Pradesh High Court has said that Vizag Hyperscale Data Centre Park Limited (VHDCPL), a special purpose vehicle owned by Adani Infra (India) Limited, may proceed with construction of an AI-ready data center campus in Visakhapatnam (Vizag), but advised that the developer proceed at its own risk.
It also said that any investment into the project could not be used as grounds to seek relief if the court ultimately rules that approvals were improperly granted.
why_it_matters_hint: Construction of a major Google-linked campus can continue but under legal risk.
notes: ET Datacenters (pool item) returned no text; W.Media relays The Times of India. The ruling date is not given.
